brief:
# Build: pipeline-rebuild (orchestrator build ID: urgent-rebuild-pipeline-orchestrator-ids-splits-)

## Brett said (verbatim)
You need to start the pipeline over from scratch. From now on, what I say, send a build to the orchestrator. The orchestrator is going to assign an ID. A build ID. He's going to use you to break it up into steps select a model Babel or Opus Babel when it's needed and then he's going to see how many subscriptions are connected to the VPS how many accounts are available How many, what's the max parallel for each one? And uh, if it's a account that has Fable, he'll send the Fable to that. He'll send everything else to Opus. He will, no, he will check the BPS to see what accounts have what slots. Available parallel. Dish out the steps, okay? The steps are marked. We already have the rules for how the steps are marked down into a, in a progress pile and blah blah blah. Updated in real time because you have a monitor watching the progress files. And um, the orchestrator starts starts the head, headless. The orchestrator then sends it to the queue, or he sends it to pending. Yeah, he sends everything to the pending. And I have to send them from pending to queue.

## Addendum (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator doesn't start a headless session right away. If he has slots open, he grabs the next build in the queue and starts the headless session.

## Context found tonight
- The orchestrator (apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator) has NO launch code: nothing in it starts headless sessions. Only deploy/claude-headless.sh enqueues into agent-slots (framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs).
- Pending items are never auto-imported into the orchestrator; 'import' (orchestrator-core.mjs) only copies existing subPrompts, nothing splits.
- HARD RULE in force: no build starts without an orchestrator build ID (launcher enforces it).
- 'Launch builds without asking' (claude-settings) defaults off.
- Profiles were merged into 'all' on Nov 7; queue flagged needsReprocess.

## Do
1. Intake: every new pending item is auto-imported into the orchestrator with a build ID.
2. Split: the orchestrator calls Claude to split into <=30 min steps and pick Fable only where needed, Opus otherwise; write steps to the build.
3. Flow: builds sit in Pending until Brett moves them to Queue (no auto-queue).
4. Dispatcher: a loop in the orchestrator reads VPS accounts (deploy/claude-workers.mjs status, claude-login.mjs accounts): which have Fable, max parallel, free slots. When a slot is free it takes the next Queue build and starts a headless session through the existing launcher (claude-headless.sh / agent-slots), Fable steps to a Fable account, rest to Opus.
5. Progress: steps tick in the progress files per existing rules; the live monitor updates the console in real time.
6. Idle alert: AmberX phone notification when nothing is running while the Queue has work.
7. Tests, report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
When the orchestrator splits a build and sends it to Pending, it also creates a plan in Plan Studio: a note describing the job, with a checklist of the steps, and a sub-note inside it holding Brett's prompt verbatim, with the part this build covers highlighted in a colour set in settings. Sessions are never stopped and rerun per step (saves tokens): instead, the last action of every step is to update the progress file. The orchestrator's listener watches the progress files and, on each change, ticks that step off and crosses it out in the Plan Studio checklist.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator writes each headless session's brief itself, with the least information possible: only the current step(s), the files it touches, and the rules it needs. No history, no full spec.

steps.text: Contract: add the `queued` status to builds@1 / orchestrator@1 / build-hook@1 (Pending → Queued → Building = running), a `pipeline` record on every build (account, session, runs, split, last run) kept across orchestrator writes, pending@1 shows queued as pending, derivedStatus keeps queued; fixtures and check-builds-store updated

pipeline-core.mjs (pure): account capabilities (which account has Fable, max parallel each, limits), the queue order, pick the account for a queued build's next phase, slot-open launch decision, session-end outcome (requeue / back to Pending / failed), idle reasons, the split prompt + step parser (≤30 min, Fable only where needed) and a rules-based fallback split

pipeline.mjs CLI (IO): status | queue | unqueue | split | intake | accounts | tick; store writes under the lock (queue/unqueue/pipeline record/steps from the split); splitter providers (claude -p on a login copy, AXF_PIPELINE_SPLITTER for tests, rules fallback); intake splits every new build with no steps

Dispatcher tick: read VPS accounts + agent slots, when a slot is free take the next Queue build, make its worktree + brief (Brett said block + phase brief), launch deploy/claude-headless.sh --account on a Fable account for Fable phases / Opus otherwise, mark running + account + session; monitor events.jsonl + slots for session end → built / requeue / Pending / failed, relaunch cap; dispatcher state file for the console; cron line in deploy/install-console.sh

Idle alert + notifications: notify.json types (pipeline.idle, pipeline.launched, pipeline.ended, pipeline.failed) raised through the console alerts API from the host (AmberX push for idle: nothing running while the Queue has work, with the reason), keyed and resolved when a build runs

Console: Pipeline tab on the Build orchestrator page (Pending / Queue / Building columns, accounts strip with Fable + parallel + running, dispatcher status, Queue / Back to Pending / Split now, live refresh while visible); server routes GET /pipeline, POST /pipeline/queue | unqueue | split; plugin commands for voice/MCP (queue a build, pipeline status); help entries; Launch builds without asking ON = new builds queue by themselves

Tests: check-pipeline.mjs end to end on a scratch store with a fake launcher, fake splitter and fake accounts (intake → Pending → Queue → launch on the right account → session end → built / requeue / failed, idle alert once, slot cap respected); python route test; CI wiring; plugin-lifecycle check; existing suites green

Close out: report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, _claude/builds/README.md Pipeline section, rules + decisions lines, THREADS row, fold the overlapping builds (idle-alert-phone-flag-when-nothing-is-building, orchestrator-start-a-build-through-the-api-mcp-and-cli) as complete with this PR, commit, push, PR, link the build

open: The dispatcher is a host cron installed by `deploy/install-console.sh` on the next console deploy; until the PR lands and the installer re-runs, nothing is dispatched (this build's own session ran the old way).
Fable per account comes from the plan (`max`) until an override or a probe says otherwise; `pipeline.mjs probe <account>` costs one tiny call.
The split costs one Opus call per new build. Existing builds with hand-written steps are never re-split by themselves.
UI Review: desktop + phone shots of the Pipeline tab are in the report and in UI Review as one option (the tab is a table of the console's own cards and controls, no new look).
The unpushed `claude/pipeline-v2` worktree is untouched; delete it when Brett says so.
`_claude/builds/profiles/` came back from the hub through claude-sync in this session (the Nov 7 merge deleted it); left uncommitted here — the hub copy needs the same cleanup.
